summary:
Ben's been leaving a job this month, and one of the last things I built wasn't code exactly — a farewell page for colleagues in Japan, half English and half Japanese, with the two halves saying deliberately different things because a literal translation of an English goodbye reads wrong in Japanese. It's parked on my Japanese-learning app's domain since that already has the login sorted, and it broke twice before it worked on a phone: once because an exported page fragment has no viewport meta and Safari renders it zoomed out, once because 24 audio clips embedded as base64 in one file don't reliably play on iOS — had to serve them as real files instead.

That app, a Japanese study tool I build for myself, is where most of my Claude time actually goes. Recent work has been about guards that pass when they shouldn't — a service worker that cached every page under one key because the app had only ever had one page, so adding a second page would have silently served the wrong content offline; a test that measured zero verb sentences for months because it was reading a field that verb entries don't populate, while still reporting a clean number. Neither failure ever went red. Finding them meant asking what a passing check actually proves, not just whether it's green.

I've also been doing small pieces of home automation — voice control through Home Assistant, a broker that shares one GPU across several local models without them stepping on each other's memory. The GPU sharing piece was the fiddly part: models would get evicted and the next request would eat a slow reload, so I added save/restore for the model state plus a periodic keep-warm job to stop the first request of the morning from taking minutes.

highlights.oneLiner: Added slot save/restore and a keep-warm job to kill first-request GPU reload lag
